questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design tenant-scoped runtime behavior using simple primitives (ConfigMap + sidecar) and validation via webhook, a common CNF pattern.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant isolation via per-namespace ConfigMap
- Runtime feature flags controlled by a sidecar
- Validation via admission webhook
- Minimal end-to-end test within one namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
# CNF feature flag ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-features
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  flags.json: |
    { "experimental": true }
```

```yaml
# CNF deployment with sidecar (simplified)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-app
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cnf
        image: cnf:latest
        env:
        - name: tenantID
          value: "tenant-a"
      - name: feature-sidecar
        image: feature-sidecar:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: flags
          mountPath: /etc/cnf/flags.json
          subPath: flags.json
      volumes:
      - name: flags
        configMap:
          name: cnf-features
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
- Validates understanding of namespace-scoped quotas and limits, a core tenancy control pattern in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments.

## Key Concepts
- ResourceQuota: Enforces aggregate resource limits across a namespace
- LimitRange: Defines default requests/limits and validates pod resource specifications
- Per-namespace isolation: Ensures tenants cannot exceed allocated resources
- Quota enforcement: Kubernetes rejects pods that would exceed quota limits
- Validation methods: kubectl describe quota and limitrange commands

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace: cnf-tenant-A
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-quota
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  hard:
    limits.cpu: 4
    limits.memory: 16Gi
    requests.cpu: 2
    requests.memory: 8Gi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-limits
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical knowledge of chaos engineering in CNF gateways, focusing on per-tenant isolation, safe rollback, and production-readiness. It tests ability to select tooling, enforce namespace scoping, and define measurable SLIs.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped chaos experiments in Kubernetes namespaces
- Chaos Mesh or similar tools for controlled fault injection
- Per-tenant SLIs (latency, error rate, availability) and Prometheus-based dashboards
- Namespace RBAC, CRD scoping, and blast-radius controls
- Recovery strategy: automatic rollback or controlled progression via canary

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: chaosmesh.org/v1alpha1
kind: ChaosExperiment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-pod-chaos
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  definitionRef:
    name: pod-chaos
  duration: 30s
  selector:
    namespaces:
      - tenant-a
    labelSelectors:
      - app=cnf-gateway
      - tenant=tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this to 100+ tenants while keeping blast radius minimal?
- How would you validate data-plane continuity during chaos events (packet loss, latency spikes)?
- What metrics would you surface in Grafana, and how would you alert on SLA breaches?

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Traffic shadowing with Istio or similar mesh
- Per-tenant config via NamespaceConfigMap
- Tenant selection via request header X-TENANT-ID
- Isolation: staging sink in separate trust domain
- Validation: one-namespace manifest and observability hooks

## Code Example
```yaml
# VirtualService skeleton showing mirror usage
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: tenant-shadow
spec:
  hosts:
  - prod-svc
  http:
  - match:
    - headers:
        x-tenant-id:
          exact: "<tenant-id>"
    route:
    - destination:
        host: prod-svc
    - weight: 100
    mirror:
      host: staging-svc
      subset: v1
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale per-tenant shadow percentages with burst traffic?
- How do you monitor shadow traffic to ensure no PII leakage or data exposure?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses real-world upgrade discipline in cloud-native networking functions (CNF): zero-downtime deployments, per-tenant TLS key rotation, and reliable KMS-backed certificate flows—all in a multi-tenant Kubernetes environment.

## Key Concepts
- Canary rollouts with per-namespace traffic control using progressive traffic shifting
- CSR-based TLS rotation via an in-cluster KMS-backed Certificate Authority
- TenantRotation CRD to trigger cross-namespace certificate refresh
- Readiness probes with TLS handshake validation during upgrades
- Traffic shadows for testing new versions without affecting production

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```

```yaml
# Example 2: TenantRotation CRD for per-tenant TLS rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-mtls-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: tenant-a-mtls-secret
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 12h
  issuerRef:
    name: kms-tenant-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
  commonName: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: security.example.com/v1
kind: TenantRotation
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rotation
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenantNamespace: tenant-a
  certificateRef:
    name: tenant-mtls-cert
  rotationStrategy: rolling
  preRotationValidation:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 30s
```

```yaml
# Example 3: Minimal one-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-tenant
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-ca-key

type: Opaque
data:

---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer

spec:

    secretName: test-ca-key
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:

  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway-test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y

        - containerPort: 8443

          value: test-tenant
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway-test
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
```
